stories.headline: US and Iran Agree to 2-Week Ceasefire With 88 Minutes to Spare Before Trump Deadline

key_facts.fact: Trump agreed to suspend attacks on Iran for two weeks, conditional on Iran immediately reopening the Strait of Hormuz, announced on Truth Social with 88 minutes left before his 8 PM EDT deadline.
key_facts.excerpt: The development came with only 88 minutes to spare before the expiration of a deadline that Mr Trump had set.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz will be possible for two weeks via coordination with Iran's Armed Forces.
key_facts.excerpt: For a period of two weeks, safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz will be possible via co-ordination with Iran's Armed Forces and with due consideration of technical limitations.

key_facts.fact: Iran's 10-point plan includes US non-aggression commitment, continued Iranian control of Hormuz, acceptance of uranium enrichment, lifting all sanctions, and withdrawal of US combat forces from the region.
key_facts.excerpt: The plan includes a US commitment to 'non-aggression', continued Iranian control over the Strait of Hormuz, acceptance of uranium enrichment, lifting all sanctions, the withdrawal of US combat forces from the region.

key_facts.fact: Pakistan mediated the deal; PM Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir were instrumental. Negotiations will begin Friday in Islamabad.
key_facts.excerpt: The Supreme National Security Council said that negotiations will begin on Friday in Islamabad.

key_facts.fact: The US-Israeli war has killed more than 5,200 people, most of them in Iran and Lebanon. The UAE has intercepted more than 2,500 Iranian projectiles.
key_facts.excerpt: The US-Israeli war has killed more than 5,200 people, most of them in Iran and Lebanon, and energy sites across the region have been bombed. The UAE has intercepted more than 2,500 projectiles.

key_facts.fact: Earlier on Tuesday, Trump warned 'a whole civilisation will die tonight' unless Iran made a deal, drawing criticism from Democrats and calls for his removal.
key_facts.excerpt: He had set a deadline for 20:00 EDT on Tuesday, threatening that 'a whole civilisation will die tonight' if no deal was reached.

stories.headline: Oil Prices Plunge ~15% and Asian Stocks Surge After US-Iran Ceasefire Deal

key_facts.fact: Brent crude fell about 13% to $94.80 per barrel, while US-traded WTI oil dropped more than 15% to $95.75 after the ceasefire announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: The price of benchmark Brent crude fell by about 13% to $94.80 a barrel, while US-traded oil was more than 15% lower at $95.75.

key_facts.fact: Oil prices remain significantly elevated from pre-conflict levels of around $70/barrel when the war started on February 28.
key_facts.excerpt: But oil prices remain higher than before the conflict started on 28 February. At the time, it was trading at around $70 a barrel.

key_facts.fact: Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 5%, South Korea's Kospi jumped nearly 6%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose 2.8%, and Australia's ASX 200 gained 2.7%.
key_facts.excerpt: Japan's Nikkei 225 gained by 5% while South Korea's Kospi jumped by nearly 6%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng was up by 2.8%, while the ASX 200 in Australia gained 2.7%.

key_facts.fact: Analysts warn it could take months for Middle East energy production to resume due to infrastructure damage, with repairs estimated at over $25 billion by Rystad Energy.
key_facts.excerpt: It could take years to fix the damage and cost more than $25bn, according to research firm Rystad Energy.

key_facts.fact: The Philippines declared a national energy emergency on March 24 after petrol prices more than doubled, as it imports 98% of its oil from the Middle East.
key_facts.excerpt: The Philippines, which imports 98% of its oil from the Middle East, became the first country to declare a national energy emergency after petrol prices more than doubled.

stories.headline: FBI, NSA, and CISA Warn Iran-Linked Hackers Are Targeting US Water and Energy Infrastructure

key_facts.fact: A joint advisory from the FBI, NSA, CISA, and other agencies warns that Iran-affiliated cyber actors are targeting internet-connected operational technology devices across US critical infrastructure sectors.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. Intelligence agencies have issued an urgent warning to private-sector companies nationwide, alerting them that Iranian-affiliated cyber actors are targeting internet-connected OT devices.

key_facts.fact: The attackers are specifically targeting Rockwell Automation and Allen-Bradley programmable logic controllers (PLCs) used in water and energy systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian-affiliated cyber actors are targeting US critical infrastructure, government says.

key_facts.fact: The campaign has had disruptive and costly effects on targeted systems, according to the advisory, as Iran retaliates against US infrastructure amid the ongoing military conflict.
key_facts.excerpt: A hacking campaign hitting industrial control systems across the United States, including energy and water utilities, that US agencies say has had disruptive and costly effects.

key_facts.fact: CISA released a dedicated cybersecurity advisory with technical indicators and mitigation guidance for operators of internet-facing industrial control devices.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian-affiliated cyber actors are targeting internet-connected OT devices, including Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley PLCs, across critical infrastructure sectors.

stories.headline: UK Exposes Russia's APT28 Hijacking MikroTik and TP-Link Routers for Global Credential Theft

key_facts.fact: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) revealed that Russian military intelligence group APT28 (Fancy Bear) is compromising popular internet routers from MikroTik, TP-Link, and other manufacturers.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian government-linked hackers are compromising popular internet routers to steal passwords for email accounts and other online services.

key_facts.fact: APT28 rewrote DNS settings on compromised routers and redirected traffic for credential theft at scale, impacting victims globally.
key_facts.excerpt: The group compromised MikroTik and TP-Link devices, rewrote DNS settings, and redirected traffic for credential theft at scale.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft published a companion security advisory detailing technical indicators of compromise from the APT28 router campaign.
key_facts.excerpt: APT28 ran a global router hijack to steal credentials.

key_facts.fact: Lumen Technologies, which operates one of the world's largest internet backbone networks, also contributed research on the campaign's infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian GRU hitting poorly made, badly secured MikroTik and TP-Link routers for intelligence gathering.

stories.headline: Tech Layoffs Hit 78,557 in Q1 2026, Nearly Half Attributed to AI Automation

key_facts.fact: Tech layoffs totaled 78,557 in Q1 2026, with the US accounting for 76.7% of cuts, according to RationalFX data cited by Nikkei Asia.
key_facts.excerpt: The true impact of artificial intelligence on employment is yet to be felt even as the global tech industry shed nearly 80,000 jobs in the first quarter.

key_facts.fact: Nearly half of the Q1 layoffs were attributed to AI implementation and workflow automation, making it the leading cited reason for job cuts.
key_facts.excerpt: Nearly half were attributed to AI implementation and workflow automation.

key_facts.fact: The Challenger Report recorded 52,050 tech job cuts through March 2026, the worst start to a year since 2023, with March alone adding 18,720 departures — up 25% from February.
key_facts.excerpt: Challenger Report data reveals 52,050 tech job cuts through March 2026, the worst start since 2023. March alone added 18,720 tech departures, up 25 percent from February.

key_facts.fact: AI was the leading single reason for March layoffs, responsible for 15,341 job cuts according to the Challenger Report, though cumulative YTD figures still rank market conditions above AI.
key_facts.excerpt: AI appeared as the leading single reason for March, responsible for 15,341 job cuts.

key_facts.fact: An NBER survey of 6,000 executives found 80% saw no employment impact from AI yet, forecasting only a 0.7% workforce reduction over three years — far below current layoff rhetoric.
key_facts.excerpt: An NBER survey of 6,000 executives found 80 percent saw no employment impact from AI yet. In contrast, they forecast only a 0.7 percent reduction over three years, far below current layoff rhetoric.

stories.headline: Hermeus Raises $350M to Build Unmanned Hypersonic Fighters, Hits $1B Valuation

key_facts.fact: Hermeus raised $200M in equity led by Khosla Ventures, with participation from Founders Fund, In-Q-Tel, RTX Ventures, Cox Enterprises, and Destiny Tech100, plus $150M in debt.
key_facts.excerpt: The Los Angeles-based startup said it has raised $200 million in equity financing, led by Khosla Ventures. The remaining $150 million comes in the form of debt.

key_facts.fact: The funding pushed Hermeus to a $1 billion valuation. The startup is developing what it calls the 'fastest unmanned aircraft,' aiming for Mach 5 speeds.
key_facts.excerpt: Defense startup Hermeus has raised $350 million to keep developing what it calls the 'fastest unmanned aircraft,' in a funding round that has pushed its valuation to $1 billion.

key_facts.fact: Hermeus flew an F-16-sized demonstrator aircraft last month and is working with RTX subsidiary Pratt & Whitney's F100 engine instead of developing a proprietary engine.
key_facts.excerpt: Last month, Hermeus flew a demonstrator version of its technology that was the size of an F-16 fighter aircraft. Piplica and his team decided to work with RTX subsidiary Pratt & Whitney to modify the F100 engine.

key_facts.fact: VC investment in defense tech crossed $9 billion over 265 rounds globally in 2025, with corporate investors contributing $2 billion across 28 rounds, according to PitchBook.
key_facts.excerpt: VC investment in defense tech crossed $9 billion over 265 rounds globally last year, according to PitchBook.

stories.headline: FDIC Proposes Regulatory Framework for Stablecoin Issuers Under GENIUS Act

key_facts.fact: The FDIC Board of Directors voted to propose a rule establishing requirements for FDIC-supervised stablecoin issuers, including standards for reserve assets.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDIC voted to propose a rule that would set forth standards for stablecoin issuers, including requirements involving reserve assets.

key_facts.fact: The proposed rule implements provisions of the GENIUS Act, which established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins pegged to the US dollar.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDIC voted to propose a rule that would set forth standards for stablecoin issuers, including requirements involving reserve assets, following GENIUS enactment.

key_facts.fact: The framework covers requirements related to reserve assets, capital, liquidity, and operational standards that FDIC-supervised institutions must meet to issue stablecoins.
key_facts.excerpt: FDIC proposes ruleset for stablecoin issuers following GENIUS enactment.
